content.text:
AI Server Demand Sustains Memory Contract Price Increases in 4Q26, While Consumer-Side Pressure Persists, Says TrendForce: TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices up 10–15% QoQ and NAND Flash up 15–20% QoQ in 4Q26. It says enterprise SSDs are the only category expected to accelerate price growth, while server DRAM remains undersupplied; it also notes weak consumer demand, constrained client SSD procurement, and LTA mechanisms that may temper some suppliers’ increases. (time=2026-09-30T04:00:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
AI Server Demand Continues to Support Memory Prices in 3Q26, but Gains Moderate as Consumer Demand Weakens and High Base Effects Take Hold, Says TrendForce: TrendForce’s 3Q26 forecast was conventional DRAM contract prices up 13–18% QoQ and NAND Flash up 10–15% QoQ. It described DRAM as undersupplied while weaker consumer demand and a higher comparison base moderated expected gains. (time=2026-07-03; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).

content.text:
DRAM Market Bulletin - Sep. 23, 2026: The public report page is dated Sep. 23 and its abstract says tight supply and robust CSP demand led TrendForce to lift its 4Q26 DRAM contract-price outlook. The public abstract does not show the revised numerical range. (time=2026-09-23; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
4Q26 Memory Price Forecast: The report page gives a Sep. 24 date and describes AI/CSP-led DRAM and NAND price increases alongside weak consumer demand. Its abstract specifies 4Q26 enterprise SSD contract-price growth of 23–28% QoQ and overall NAND growth of 15–20% QoQ; the displayed abstract does not give the conventional DRAM range. (time=2026-09-24; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
